Fallout Shelter should be out on Android in August!

Honestly, I probably will lose interest in the game by August. I'm hearing how there's absolutely nothing to do once you get to the late stages of the game. Bethesda shot themselves in the foot IMO when they limited their audience during launch and to make the endgame completely pointless.

However, I would like to hear from people who have played it. Is it worth it?

You are absolutely right regarding the fat burnout rate. I got to the upper levels early on and haven't been back in days. In fact, I think I left one of my favorite vault dwellers to wander the wastelands days ago and now he's probably passed on, oh no! :( But I don't regret playing and it really was a blast until I filled up the joint.
At least it's fun in the beginning. Just curious - how long did it take you to get to the later stages of the game?

I used a cheat in which I played around with my time/date settings to can boost past time related events. Because of that I probably finished faster than most. It took me maybe a week? And mind you I was boosting so I do think you could definitely get a couple of weeks of solid gameplay out of it.

If you consider a population of 200 (which is the current cap) as finished then it is super easy to reach large population. The dwellers are quite a randy bunch and it is VERY easy to overpopulate. The main thing is to be mindful of your resources and use your bottle caps wisely. If you do wind up playing the game I suggest looking at the upgrades you can purchase later in the game. I wound up spending a lot of caps on upgrading low level rooms instead of waiting to unlock higher level rooms later in the game and I really regret that.

Really good information. Thanks! I was completely unaware that the game could last a good few weeks even with the weak endgames. Apparently I was under the impression that it was a game where it's fun for a few days and then you never touch it again.

I'll see what the reviews are for the Android version. Hopefully it's a smooth launch with little to no bugs so that I can start playing it immediately.

The only reason why I say it could take weeks is because you have tasks you need to accomplish that take hours (in the real world) to complete. So while actual gameplay itself may not last that long you have to wait for characters/rooms to level up or acquire goods.

Which is fine for me. I'm not expecting to constantly play on my phone with terrible battery life for hours on end. I think most of my games that I have on my phone are similar types - play for any time between a few minutes to half an hour, exit, forget about it for a few hours - days until upgrades complete, play some more, etc.

They really did shoot themselves in the foot when they released it just to IOS. Unless they bring more content when they release the android version, I don't know that it will have as much popularity or excitement.

I have a chatty, oblivious old lady that always writes checks. She always manages to come into an empty store but the minute she puts her first arm load of soda, chips, and other hot trash on the counter ten people walk in behind her, and out of politeness wait for the hag to finish her shopping, as she brings forward armload after armload to the pile at my register. Once rung up she fishes her checkbook from her overstuffed purse, writes the total and the date (which she cant remember and asks for) in the front of the checkbook and then writes out the total on the check. Then writes the store name and a little memo, before asking for the date again, dating the check, and ever-so-carefully folding the check over the perforation and tearing the check loose. Happy and slightly demented as this old lady is, she is sure to take lots of time out of this process to test my skills at small talk. So I have a little small talk performance in front of ten impatient people, for a total of eleven people fantasizing about doing violent harm to an old lady, and probably about ten who include me in their violent and unerotic daydream.

Then I get to feed the check into the reader that then communicates all the check data via smoke signal to the comcast customer service email address, where it is then eventually forwarded on to a credit card company that grinds to a halt as the usually automated system has to be hand operated because of how outdated checks are.

When they finish and decide that the old ladies' skimpy bank account can just afford to lose seventeen dollars, I get a conformation at my terminal. Then I hand the check to the lady, she signs it, and hands it back to me. Then, and only then, does she begin packing back the ream of paper that somehow fell out of her purse onto the counter during this process. She secures the scraps into various tiny zipper pockets, then carefully as if disarming a bomb, grabs the five sacks of garbage in front of her, forgetting her keys or wallet or credit-card she didn't use for some reason on the counter as she slowly waddles away.

See you tomorrow, Grace.
Witcher 3 Patch 1.07 coming soon to all platforms

Such a huge patch...Here are the notes:

  • A new, alternative (optional) movement response mode for Geralt.
  • A player stash for storing items, available in various locations throughout the game. Stash locations are marked on the player's map.
  • Crafting and alchemy components no longer add to the overall inventory weight.
  • Books are now placed in a dedicated tab in the Inventory and books that have already been read are properly grayed out.
  • Multiple sorting options are now available in the Inventory.
  • Alchemy formulas and crafting diagrams can be "pinned", meaning all components and ingredients required to make them will be conveniently marked in the Shop panel.
  • Dozens of fixes for quest related issues, both major and minor.
  • A few performance enhancements, including the optimization of FX, scenes and general gameplay.
  • Various improvements to horse behavior.
